title: Growing up with Lionel Hampton and Milt Hinton
summary: They shared a neighborhood; Wilson's violin lessons led Hinton's parents to start him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Made a score, and then transposed it? Lionel Hampton made a nice record of "Blue Because of You."
Yeah.
Beautiful record. Did you know Hampton was in Chicago?
Knew Hamp, I was raised up with Hamp.
Really?
That's right. He was -- we were both in the same neighborhood. Lionel Hampton, Milt Hinton and myself, and a piano player by the name of Raymond Walters.
This is in the Englewood --
No, this was down the road there. We moved from Englewood when I was five years old. This was 37th and Rhodes.
37th and Rhodes?
Yeah.
Yeah, I worked with Milt this spring, and he was talking about going back to the old neighborhood.
I know he didn't recognize it, because it's all different. That's all tore down.
Yeah. He said it was pretty un-
comfortable. Said he used to deliver papers down there on the Southside.
Uh-huh. I'm the cause of Milt Hinton being in music.
How's that?

When I started taking lessons from Sanborn, and the other guys wanted to start taking violin lessons, so Milt Hinton's parents gave him violin lessons, and gave another friend of mine, lived around the corner from me, violin. ABout four or five pupils he had just through me.
I'll be darned. And then two of you went on to the string bass. Well, what kind of kid was Hampton?
Oh, great. Great. Great.
Was he always --

We used to, you know -- I had my fiddle, and he'd have an old piece of drum. We'd be out on the curb stomp-playing. And he'd be running all up and down the curb with his drumsticks, drumming on the curb stones. He was doing that before Barrett (Deems) . Drumming on the picket fences, and things. Yeah. Humming. He always did that hum.
Really?
Yeah, he always did that. Yeah.
Well, he left Chicago and ended out on the West Coast?
Yeah, ended up in California. That's when I lost track of him.
